thread.title: Stephen F. Austin and McNeese to face off in Southland Conference title game
thread.title_full: Stephen F. Austin and McNeese to face off in Southland Conference title game

author: b. p. castaneda
title: Stephen F. Austin and McNeese to face off in Southland Conference title game
text:
Stephen F. Austin will play against McNeese for the Southland Conference championship and an automatic bid to the NCAA Tournament on March 11 in Lake Charles. The two teams, seeded first and second respectively, will meet for the third time this season at Townsley Law Arena, where McNeese previously won by a narrow margin.
The matchup is significant as it determines not only conference supremacy but also which team advances to the national tournament. Both teams have had strong seasons, with Stephen F. Austin securing its first regular season conference title since a three-way finish atop the Western Athletic Conference standings in 2021-22 and its first outright Southland Conference title since 2019-20.
In their last outing, Stephen F. Austin advanced to the final after Keon Thompson intercepted a pass and scored a go-ahead basket with just over twelve seconds remaining, helping his team secure a 60-58 victory over Texas A&M-Corpus Christi. The win allowed the Jacks to continue their pursuit of another conference tournament title.
This season has seen several milestones for Stephen F. Austin. The team became the first in league history to win 20 conference games in a single season, setting a new program record for victories within one campaign. Additionally, both Stephen F. Austin and McNeese finished with more than 25 wins each—another first for the league.
McNeese enters the championship as defending tournament champions and are currently on a nine-game winning streak following a triple-overtime victory against UTRGV. Their roster features standout players such as Larry Johnson, Tyshawn Archie, and Garwey Dual, who have contributed to leading statistics in scoring offense and defensive categories within the conference.
Several members of Stephen F. Austin received individual honors from the league: Keon Thompson was named Player of the Year; Jerald Colonel earned Defensive Player of the Year; Lateef Patrick was recognized as Newcomer of the Year; and head coach Matt Braeuer was awarded Coach of the Year.
